extracted.intended_audience: K01 career development award applicants, mentors, and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: NIH Summary Statement guidance and reviewer criteria used to evaluate a K01 Mentored Research Scientist Development Award application, covering Candidate, Career Development, Research Plan, Mentorship, Environment, human subjects/inclusion, and related administrative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Based upon the evaluation of scientific and technical merit, this application received an Overall Impact/Priority score of 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. See NIH peer review process guidance at http://grants.nih.gov/grants/peer_review_process.htm#scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the applicant's qualifications, training, productivity, and potential to become an independent investigator (e.g., 'The candidate is outstanding and has a Ph.D. in Epidemiology... published extensively... recognized as an emerging expert').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider training background (degrees), publication record, prior related work, mentorship relationships, and demonstrated commitment to the field. Reviewers listed specific strengths (strong publication record, relevant experience) and noted 'None' for weaknesses when appropriate. Numerical reviewer ratings (e.g., '1') are used to reflect the assessment (lower = better).

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals & Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the quality and appropriateness of the applicant's career development and training plan (courses, mentorship, planned activities) and how it supports career goals (e.g., 'well-developed career development plan centered around a multidisciplinary mentorship team and selected course work').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the plan follows logically from prior work, includes appropriate didactic training (e.g., advanced biostatistics, health policy/economics coursework), integration with mentors, opportunities for external interactions (e.g., HRSA, CDC meetings), and whether weaknesses identified in prior reviews were addressed. Reviewers may assign numeric scores (e.g., '1' = excellent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges the scientific merit, clarity, feasibility, and novelty of the proposed research (e.g., aims to quantify disparities in Care Continuum outcomes using NA-ACCORD and CCASAnet data; aims 1–3 listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider appropriateness of aims, use of preliminary data, data sources and their strengths (large longitudinal cohorts), analytic approach, novelty (filling geographic/contextual gaps), and potential weaknesses (e.g., challenges comparing data across countries and cohorts). Reviewers provided strengths (robust databases, well-constructed aims) and noted potential minor concerns; numerical ratings are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the expertise, commitment, and fit of the mentoring and collaborator team (e.g., 'lead mentor is a recognized leader... added mentors in biostatistics... outstanding letters of support').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mentors' relevant track records (e.g., K24 awardees, R01-funded investigators), presence of local statistical mentorship, institutional roles, and demonstrated commitment to the candidate. Strengths/weaknesses should be noted; reviewers scored this dimension (e.g., '1').

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the research environment, institutional support, and commitments (e.g., 'Vanderbilt University presents an excellent research environment... strong letter of commitment from the Infectious Disease Division Director').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional resources, protected time, collaborations, and letters indicating support. Reviewers list strengths and may note absence of weaknesses. Numerical scoring is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission / Response to Prior Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the applicant addressed weaknesses from prior review and improved the application (e.g., 'The candidate is very responsive to previous critiques, and he addresses and satisfactorily answers all concerns... The candidate has addressed all weaknesses identified in the first review').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that specific prior criticisms were addressed (methodological, training, mentorship) and that revisions strengthen the application; positive resubmission adjustments are considered in scoring. Note NIH guidance on resubmissions (e.g., NOT-OD-14-074).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance / Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the public health importance of the research question and potential to inform policy/practice (e.g., 'The results of this study may help to inform policy makers about the impact of current health policy decisions on the HIVCC... will be of great interest and utility to epidemiologists, clinicians, and policy makers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alignment with national/international strategies (NHAS, WHO guidelines), timeliness (policy relevance such as ACA and Medicaid expansion), and potential to identify targets for interventions. This feeds into overall impact considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews protections for human subjects and whether human subjects involvement is acceptable (e.g., 'Human Subjects: 30-Human subjects involved - Certified, no SRG concerns'; 'PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS ... ACCEPTABLE (Code 30)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether protections, risks, and certification are adequate. Codes are used (e.g., Code 30 = acceptable). Reviewers note 'no SRG concerns' when protections are sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the presence and adequacy of a data and safety monitoring plan when applicable (listed under the resume sections: 'DATA AND SAFETY MONITORING PLAN - NOT APPLICABLE' in this case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, evaluate monitoring mechanisms; if not applicable, note that status. Provide acceptability codes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates plans for inclusion of women in the research ('INCLUSION OF WOMEN PLAN - ACCEPTABLE (Code G1A)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether inclusion plans meet NIH policies and are acceptable; codes denote adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates plans for inclusion of minority populations ('INCLUSION OF MINORITIES PLAN - ACCEPTABLE (Code M1A)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether inclusion plans meet NIH policies and are acceptable; codes denote adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates plans for inclusion/exclusion of children ('INCLUSION OF CHILDREN PLAN - ACCEPTABLE (Code C3A)' and elsewhere '3A-No children included, scientifically acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm justification for inclusion/exclusion of children and that the plan meets policy; use provided codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses vertebrate animal involvement ('VERTEBRATE ANIMALS - NOT APPLICABLE (Code 10)'; '10-No live vertebrate animals involved for competing appl.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If animals are involved, evaluate care and use; if not, mark not applicable and use code 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes whether biohazard issues apply ('BIOHAZARD COMMENT - NOT APPLICABLE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If biohazard materials/procedures are used, evaluate biosafety; otherwise note not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the adequacy of planned training in RCR ('TRAINING IN THE RESPONSIBLE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH ACCEPTABLE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers verify that RCR training plans are present and acceptable for the candidate and list any needed improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Institution / Select Agents / Resource Sharing / Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative/resource-related review items that note applicability and acceptability (multiple entries in this application: 'NOT APPLICABLE' for FOREIGN INSTITUTION, SELECT AGENTS, RESOURCE SHARING PLANS, AUTHENTICATION OF KEY BIOLOGICAL AND/OR CHEMICAL RESOURCES).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each administrative/resource criterion, determine applicability and adequacy of plans; if material, review the specific plans and label as acceptable/unacceptable or provide required modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews the requested budget and period of support ('The budget was recommended as requested.'; 'ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET NOTE: The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations made by reviewers... costs will be calculated by Institute grants management staff based on recommendations outlined below in the COMMITTEE BUDGET RECOMMENDATIONS section.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reasonableness of requested direct costs; note that reviewer recommendations do not equate to final award budgeting, which is handled administratively if an award is planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and Reviewer Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains reviewer scoring submission and meeting procedures ('The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that individual criterion scores are used for internal record and that the overall impact score is the primary quantitative outcome (averaged and multiplied), and that NIH policy (e.g., resubmission rules NOT-OD-14-074) affects application handling.
